expected_evidence: Geological: multi-site re-sampling of the ~12,900 cal BP (Younger Dryas onset) sediment boundary layer across North America showing iridium/platinum-group-element concentrations statistically indistinguishable from background, not anomalous spikes
Geological: failure of independent labs to reproduce reported iridium anomalies from the original Firestone et al.-type sites when re-analyzed with standard ICP-MS/INAA protocols

Material: re-examination of purported impact 'markers' (magnetic microspherules, nanodiamonds, carbon spherules) showing they are common detrital, authigenic, or anthropogenic-contamination artifacts rather than extraterrestrial ejecta

Astronomical: absence of any confirmed North American impact crater of appropriate age/size to source an iridium plume, and absence of shocked quartz or other unambiguous impact-diagnostic minerals at the boundary

Geological/paleoecological: continental charcoal and pollen records not showing a synchronous, anomalously severe biomass-burning spike or abrupt vegetation-cooling signature exceeding normal YD-onset variability (undercutting the 'biomass-burning-impact-winter' mechanism)

model_prior (unverified, from training recollection): peer-reviewed critical literature (e.g., Pinter et al. 2011 'Requiem for the Younger Dryas impact hypothesis', Holliday & Meltzer, van Hoesel et al.) reporting failed replications and methodological critiques of the original iridium-anomaly claims
response.rationale: This hypothesis concerns a *refutation* claim about the Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis (iridium anomaly at ~10,950 BCE / ~12,900 cal BP in North America). Unlike most hypotheses in this engine, the relevant 'evidence' is not ancient behavioral/cultural traces but modern geochemical and stratigraphic re-analysis of the YD boundary layer itself — a layer that is widely preserved in lake sediments, loess, and archaeological sites across North America and has been repeatedly, independently sampled since the original 2007 claim. Using the ('younger-dryas', kind) rows, the most relevant channels are geological (0.65) and astronomical (0.7, covering crater/impact-mineral searches), both comparatively high-detectability categories in this table, plus material (0.35) for microspherule/nanodiamond re-analysis and model_prior (0.3) for the surrounding scientific-literature debate (flagged as unverified, training-derived recollection, not confirmed fact). Because refutation evidence here is generated by ongoing, repeatable modern scientific sampling rather than fragile organic or textual survival, detectability is higher than the raw table average across all eight kinds would suggest — I weight geological and astronomical more heavily than genetic/linguistic/oral_tradition/iconographic/textual, which are essentially irrelevant to this geochemical dispute (textual=0.0, linguistic=0.05, oral_tradition=0.1, iconographic=0.1 for younger-dryas). A composite adjustment of ~0.55 reflects that absence of a reproducible iridium anomaly, if the hypothesis is true, is quite plausible to detect and has in fact been actively sought by researchers, so an absence-of-anomaly finding should not be dismissed as merely a detectability artifact — though some low-detectability channels (textual, linguistic, oral tradition) legitimately contribute near-zero expected evidence and their silence carries no evidentiary weight either way.
